landmarks.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
landmarks.writeup: A memorial site in Kigali dedicated to the victims of the 1994 genocide, offering educational exhibits and a place for remembrance.

wiki.extract: The Kigali Genocide Memorial commemorates the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The remains of over 250,000 people are interred there.

landmarks.name: Volcanoes National Park
landmarks.writeup: Famous for mountain gorilla tracking, this park is part of the Virunga volcanic chain and a key conservation area.

wiki.extract: Volcanoes National Park is a national park in northwestern Rwanda. It covers 160 km2 (62 sq mi) of rainforest and encompasses five of the eight volcanoes in the Virunga Mountains, namely Karisimbi, Bisoke, Muhabura, Gahinga and Sabyinyo. It borders Virunga National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Mgahinga Gorilla National Park in Uganda. It is home to the mountain gorilla and the golden monkey, and was the base for the primatologist Dian Fossey.

landmarks.name: Lake Kivu
landmarks.writeup: One of Africa's Great Lakes, known for its scenic beauty and recreational activities along the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo.

wiki.extract: Lake Kivu is one of the African Great Lakes. It lies on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, and is in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift. Lake Kivu empties into the Ruzizi River, which flows southwards into Lake Tanganyika.

landmarks.name: Nyungwe Forest National Park
landmarks.writeup: A large montane rainforest with rich biodiversity, including chimpanzees and numerous bird species.

wiki.extract: The Nyungwe Forest is located in southwestern Rwanda, on the border with Burundi, where it is contiguous with the Kibira National Park to the south, and Lake Kivu and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west. The Nyungwe rainforest is most likely the best preserved montane rainforest in Africa. It is located in the watershed between the basin of the Congo River to the west and the basin of the river Nile to the east. From the east side of the Nyungwe forest comes also one of the branches of the Nile sources.

cultural_events.name: Kwita Izina
cultural_events.writeup: An annual gorilla naming ceremony that celebrates conservation efforts and raises awareness about mountain gorillas.

wiki.extract: Kwita Izina is a Rwandan ceremony of giving a name to a newborn baby gorilla. It is named after the traditional baby naming ceremony that takes place after the birth of a newborn child in Rwandan culture.

cultural_events.name: Umuganura
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional harvest festival marking the start of the new agricultural season, celebrating community and gratitude.

wiki.extract: This is a list of public holidays in Rwanda. Rwanda observes fourteen regular public holidays, which reflects the civic, historical and religious landscape.

food_writeup: Rwandan cuisine features staple foods like beans, bananas, sweet potatoes, and maize. Dishes often include grilled meats and stews, with a focus on locally sourced ingredients.
brief_history: Rwanda, once a kingdom, was colonized by Germany and later Belgium. It gained independence in 1962. The 1994 genocide against the Tutsi resulted in massive loss of life. Since then, Rwanda has focused on reconciliation and development.
